slope: Steep ground tips a lander over. Safe landing sites need gentle slopes, so always check the slope before committing.
cold: Without sunlight the lander's batteries must keep heaters and electronics alive, and long polar nights drain them. Very cold sites are hard to survive.
blackout: Near the pole, Earth can sit below the horizon for long stretches, cutting the radio link. A site that is often in view of Earth keeps communications open.
low_sun: Solar panels need sunlight to make power. A site that stays dark for too long leaves the lander without energy.
low_comm: Communication depends on how much of the time Earth is above the horizon. Poor visibility means a patchy link with mission control.
win: Well done! You balanced slope, sunlight, temperature and Earth visibility, and the lander survived until the end of its window.
